**Group:** Dinoflagellates  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

A "desmokont" dinoflagellate whose theca is made of two large valves joined along a sagittal (lengthwise) suture, like a clam shell or shield, with no cingulum or sulcus grooves. The two flagella emerge together from an apical periflagellar area that often bears a small tooth or spine. Cells are oval, heart-, or teardrop-shaped in valve view. Key features: two-valve clam-like theca, apical flagellar pore with spine, absence of a girdle.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **dinophysis** | Dinophysis is also two-parted but bears a funnel cingular list and sail-like sulcal lists; Prorocentrum is a plain two-valved cell with an apical spine and no lists. |
| **ceratium** | Ceratium has long horns and an obvious girdle; Prorocentrum has neither. |
